quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Be ready to change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: How can you ride safely at night?

options.text: Other drivers cannot see your turn signals at night.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night. This makes other drivers able to see you.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is the correct body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
Sit as far back as possible so you have to stretch to reach the grips.
Lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips. This lets you reach and operate the controls easily and comfortably.

questions.question: What happens if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: It is fine as long as you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is fine as long as no other vehicles are near.
You may end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. If you cannot hold the turn, you may end up in another lane or off the road. Be careful when turning.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the number of drinks consumed. After four hours, about four drinks would still be in their system.

questions.question: What is switching to a lower gear also called?
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Try to blend in and not be noticed by other drivers.
Do not use turn signals except at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers. Use turn signals, brake lights, and good lane position to show your intentions. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: Which item is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves. Sandals do not protect your feet.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Slow down so any vehicle in your blind spot can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before you change lanes.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you to be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent dangerous problems. Small issues are more serious on a motorcycle than on a car.

questions.question: As a motorcycle operator, you can help others see you by:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals to increase your visibility to other drivers.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Eyeballing the tire is a good method.
It is best to squeeze the tire.
Compare the height of the tire to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. An under-inflated tire may look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: When looking for a protective jacket or pair of pants, choose items made of:
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the best protection.

questions.question: Common drugs, such as cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect your ability to safely ride your motorcycle.
Usually will not affect your ability to safely ride your motorcycle.
Pose no risk to your riding ability.
Are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to safely ride your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Check the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: For best protection, make sure your helmet:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no obvious defects.

questions.question: Your main source for information about your motorcycle should be:
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is your best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It contains details about specifications, operation, and maintenance.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in broad daylight. To be more visible, you should:
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen in daylight, wear bright clothing every time you ride, even during the day.

questions.question: What can help reduce your chance of having an accident?

options.text: Ride within one foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Signal only when you want to.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show what you are doing. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When you adjust your rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. A properly adjusted mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but the important thing is to see the road behind and to the side of you.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.explanation: You can slow down by downshifting. However, this does not turn on your brake lights, so other drivers may not know you are slowing down.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This only takes a few minutes and helps keep you safe before you ride.

questions.question: Which clothing choice is NOT good for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide the protection you need.

questions.question: How is alcohol removed from your body?
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What should you inspect during a pre-ride check?

options.text: The wear and tread on your tires

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread on your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, what should you do?

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a limit beforehand so you can still ride safely.
Not worry about riding if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: The safest choice is to not ride after drinking. Any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to ride safely.
